source_title: Good Practices in Home Kitchens: Construction and Validation of an Instrument for Household Food-Borne Disease Assessment and Prevention
article_summary: The article develops and validates a checklist for assessing good practices in home kitchens, focusing mainly on food safety, hygiene, equipment condition, food storage, water supply, waste management, lighting, and ventilation/acclimatization. Its relevance to greener smart-home rules is indirect: it can help preserve safety and comfort constraints when modifying kitchen-related automations, especially around appliance functioning, refrigeration, ventilation, water infrastructure, and household routines. The article does not focus on energy saving, sustainability, environmental feedback, or optimized automation scheduling.
